holidays.name: Alien Abduction Day
holidays.description: Also called Extraterrestrial Abduction Day. It's a tongue-in-cheek day to look up at the night sky, swap close-encounter stories, and make sure your tinfoil hat is ready. Sci-fi marathons are encouraged. Anyone with a tractor beam in the driveway should stay calm.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a favorite among fans of UFO lore and science fiction, and it falls right on the spring equinox.
holidays.funFact: The best-known alleged abduction in the U.S. is the 1961 Betty and Barney Hill case in New Hampshire. It helped shape the popular image of the alien abduction story.

holidays.name: National Ravioli Day
holidays.description: A day for stuffed pasta pillows of every kind. Cheese, spinach, pumpkin, meat and even dessert versions are all welcome. Fork optional, enthusiasm mandatory.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It honors a dish with roots in Italian cuisine that has been popular for centuries.
holidays.funFact: Ravioli dates back to at least the 14th century in Italy. Records from that era mention the stuffed pasta, and it has been a kitchen staple ever since.

holidays.name: Snowman Burning Day
holidays.description: A fiery farewell to winter. People send off their frosty friends as the spring equinox arrives, with a symbolic bonfire (or a safer, melty goodbye). It's a dramatic way to say hello to spring.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It echoes old European spring traditions that burn winter in effigy to welcome warmer days.
holidays.funFact: Zurich, Switzerland holds a similar festival called Sechseläuten. Its centerpiece is a snowman effigy called the Böögg, which is stuffed with fireworks and set alight. Townspeople say the faster its head explodes, the better the summer will be.
